risk_if_not_implemented: Without Identity Providers (IdP) & Authorization Servers, unauthorized individuals, devices or services may gain access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services, Data and/or Facilities (TAASDF). Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege (R-AC-2), Unauthorized Privilege Elevation (R-AC-3), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) organizational users and processes acting on behalf of organizational users.
compensating_control_1.justification: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users (IAC-32) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Identity Providers (IdP) & Authorization Servers (IAC-03.3) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to restrict access to individuals assigned specific roles with legitimate business needs.
compensating_control_2.justification: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) (IAC-06) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Identity Providers (IdP) & Authorization Servers (IAC-03.3) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
